title: Electoral Legislation Amendment (Annual Disclosure Equality) Bill 2021
short_title: Electoral Legislation Amendment (Annual Disclosure Equality) Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would apply the same donation rules to all federal politicians, whether they are currently in office or running for election.
Sitting parliamentarians would have to report gifts they receive directly for federal election purposes each year to the Australian Electoral Commission.
The period during which someone is treated as a candidate for disclosure and foreign donation rules would be lengthened by six months.
changes: Extends the foreign donations ban to cover the entire term of a sitting member, not just after they announce a re-election bid.
Requires parliamentarians who receive gifts directly for federal election purposes to lodge an annual return with the AEC.
Increases the candidate disclosure period by six months for returns and foreign donation restrictions.
summary.affected: Sitting members of the House of Representatives and the Senate, and candidates for federal election.

According to the [bill homepage](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/Bills_Search_Results/Result?bId=r6818), the bill was introduced to: * *extend the application of the foreign donations framework to current sitting members of the House of Representatives and Senators;* * *require members of the House of Representatives and Senators who receive gifts for the purpose of incurring electoral expenditure or creating or communicating electoral matter to lodge an annual return with the Australian Electoral Commission; and* * *extend the period for which a person is taken to be a candidate by an additional six months for the purpose of the disclosure period for candidate and Senate group returns and for restrictions on receiving foreign donations.*

speeches.speaker: Tim Wilson
speeches.brief: The Electoral Legislation Amendment (Annual Disclosure Equality) Bill 2021 requires all parliamentarians, including independents, to lodge annual returns on political donations and prohibits them from receiving gifts of $1,000 or more from foreign donors. It also extends disclosure obligations for candidates and Senate groups to six months before announcing candidacy.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Giles
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Electoral Legislation Amendment (Annual Disclosure Equality) Bill 2021, which extends the ban on foreign donations to sitting parliamentarians and requires them to submit annual returns of donations over the disclosure threshold of $14,500. The speaker also moved an amendment calling for the disclosure threshold to be lowered to $1,000, real-time disclosure, and a national anti-corruption commission.

speeches.speaker: James Stevens
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Electoral Legislation Amendment (Annual Disclosure Equality) Bill 2021 but opposed the amendment, arguing that independent MPs should be subject to the same donation disclosure requirements as political parties, including the $14,500 threshold and the ban on foreign donations.

speeches.speaker: Zali Steggall
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the government's Electoral Legislation Amendment (Annual Disclosure Equality) Bill 2021 is hypocritical, imposing extra disclosure on independents while major parties hide donations through party returns and blind trusts, and noted the loophole was identified by the independent member for Indi. They called for genuine reform including lowering the donation threshold from $14,500 to $1,000, real-time reporting, truth in political advertising, and a federal integrity commission, citing that 55% of ALP and 65% of coalition donations were undisclosed.

speeches.speaker: Jason Falinski
speeches.brief: The speaker contributed to the debate on the Electoral Legislation Amendment (Annual Disclosure Equality) Bill 2021, thanking Deputy Speaker Freelander. No specific policy positions, figures, or names were stated.

speeches.speaker: Helen Haines
speeches.brief: The speaker welcomed the bill's transparency measures but criticised the government for failing to consult the crossbench and for ignoring loopholes exploited by major parties, and announced amendments to lower the donation disclosure threshold from $14,500 to $1,000 and require parties to report candidate-specific funding when a candidate submits a nil return.

speeches.speaker: Ken Wyatt
speeches.brief: The Electoral Legislation Amendment (Annual Disclosure Equality) Bill 2021 will extend foreign donation restrictions to parliamentarians for their full term, require annual returns to the AEC for direct donations, and extend the candidate disclosure period by six months to improve electoral transparency and integrity.
